_comment: Template for ONE RESEARCH PASS (a shard), written to strains/<strain_id>/<shard>.json. The filename follows body_systems: all.json when one pass covered all six, otherwise gi / immune / metabolic / mental-health / mechanistic / safety. EVERY claim below is a worked example, not a finding: delete them all and write your own - an example row left behind validates cleanly and publishes an invented finding. A shard carries strain_id and NOTHING else about the entity - genus, species, designation, aliases and component strains live only in ../roster.json and are joined at build time. A claim carries impact_id and NO other outcome field - the label and body system live only in ../vocabulary/outcomes.json and are joined at build time. Do not add either set back to a file. searched_empty lists the impact_ids this pass individually searched and could not write a row for; it starts empty here on purpose, because an example id left behind would record a search that never ran. A deep pass's remaining debt is derived as allowed ids minus claimed minus searched_empty, so record every empty targeted search - an unrecorded one re-opens the pass. See ../SCHEMA.md for field definitions, tier rules, and validation rules.
pass_summary: 2-4 sentences on what THIS pass covered: best-supported findings, where the evidence is weakest, any safety signal worth knowing. Plain language. Must not depend on a sibling shard - that independence is what lets passes run in parallel - except in the safety pass, the entity's closing pass, which runs last and reads its siblings for harm signals. A pass that found nothing gradeable still writes this file, with claims: [] and a summary saying what was searched and came back empty.

claims._comment: Human row scoped to a sub-population under tier rule 5, and the worked example of aggregation: the SR pools 8 trials, 2 more were published after it, so study_type carries both, n_studies/n_participants cover all 10, and effect_size names the 8 it actually came from.
claims.tier_rationale: Why this tier, what was downgraded or upgraded and why, and - where sub-populations diverge - which went which way. E.g. 'Cochrane SR, low heterogeneity, RoB assessed. Two later RCTs consistent in direction, not pooled. Adult evidence separately pooled and null; row scoped to children per tier rule 5.'
claims.dose: 1x10^9-2x10^10 CFU/day across pooled trials; effect concentrated at >=1x10^10
claims.safety_flags: Anything specific to this claim's population, or empty string.
claims.notes: Only what genuinely does not fit a field above.

claims._comment: Tier rule 6, middle case - the most error-prone row in the catalogue. The only SR pools across a whole genus, so its RR is NOT this strain's finding. What it does give is this strain's own trials, listed with RoB ratings, so the row is graded from those: study_type human_rct, bias_assessment sr_assessed (bias really was appraised), and validation rule 6 caps it at B because human_meta is absent. Taking the pooled RR here instead would fabricate a tier A row.
claims.effect_size: incidence RR 0.71 [0.52-0.98] in the largest trial; not pooled at strain level
claims.tier_rationale: Only SR pools across Lactobacillus spp.; pooled estimate not attributable to this strain per tier rule 6. Graded from the 3 strain-specific trials in its included-studies table, all rated low/some-concerns RoB. Caps at B without a strain-level meta-analysis.

claims._comment: Preclinical row. A humans row and an animals row may share an impact_id - what may never repeat is the (impact_id, population) pair, across the whole entity directory rather than one file. Tier is P by definition for any animals or in_vitro row. In a deep entity this row lives in mechanistic.json, never in gi.json.
claims.tier_rationale: Preclinical only. Tier P by definition; strength is carried by n_studies, consistency, and independently_replicated, not by the tier.

claims._comment: Safety row. direction is 'harm', and human safety signals are usually case reports - human_case_report, tier D. Do not code these as human_observational: that value implies a comparison group and would contradict the tier. n_participants is null, not 0: case reports have no denominator, and 0 would read as a measured zero.
claims.population_detail: immunocompromised patients, central venous catheter, short bowel syndrome
claims.tier_rationale: Case reports only; no denominator, so incidence is unknown. Tier D reflects study design, not the seriousness of the outcome.
claims.safety_flags: Who should not take this, and why.

proposed_impacts.suggested_label: Only if a real finding has NO matching id in vocabulary/outcomes.json. Check excluded_outcomes first.
proposed_impacts.rationale: Why no existing id fits. Do NOT mint an impact_id here. suggested_body_system is kept even though claim rows carry no body system: a proposal has no vocabulary row to join one from yet, and the suggestion is the input to writing that row.

gaps: Optional narrative: why a searched_empty id came back empty, notable questions found unstudied, trials underway.
